questions.question: Calculate all five profitability percentages for Zanele's year and read them as one dashboard.
questions.expected_answer: Gross profit on sales: 20 000/60 000 × 100 = 33,3%. Gross profit on cost of sales: 20 000/40 000 × 100 = 50% — the mark-up, confirming the pricing policy. Operating expenses on sales: 15 200/60 000 × 100 = 25,3%. Operating profit on sales: 12 000/60 000 × 100 = 20%. Net profit on sales: 10 500/60 000 × 100 = 17,5%. Dashboard: of every hundred rand of sales, about sixty-seven replaces the goods, thirty-three is margin, twenty-five runs the shop, twenty survives the operations and seventeen-fifty reaches the owner after the financing bite of two and a half.

questions.question: Explain why gross profit is read against two bases, and what a gap between achieved and policy mark-up signals.
questions.expected_answer: The same gross profit is the mark-up when read on cost (what was added on) and the margin when read on sales (what was received) — the two ends of the counter. If the policy says 50% on cost but the achieved percentage computes lower, say 44%, the gap is a finding: possible markdowns or sales below full price, stock lost, broken or stolen after costing, recording errors, or theft of takings. The percentage cannot name the culprit but raises the alarm and sizes the leak — the most heavily tested interpretation at this level.

questions.question: Write the anatomy of a full interpretation comment and illustrate it on a falling margin.
questions.expected_answer: Four moves: STATE the figure with its comparison ('gross profit on sales fell from 36% to 33,3%'); JUDGE it ('a deterioration — nearly three rand less from every hundred to work with'); EXPLAIN from the scenario ('consistent with the clearance sale mentioned, or stock damaged after costing'); RECOMMEND one action ('count stock against the books; review the discount depth'). The why must come from supplied clues, not imagination, and the comment must come from the right gauge — gross percentages for pricing/stock questions, the expense percentage for cost management, net on sales for the overall keep.
